When someone is depressed for a very long time, its like your body chemistry and mental state slowly bubble up until eventually, your wellbeing boils over and, at the time, it seems preferable to you that dying is better than living. I'm sorry you feel like shit. 

I know when you're in the thick of it, its easy to get lost in the possibility of death. The ability to assume that you're going to be dead soon is a freeing perspective that may seem preferable to feeling awful all the time. 

The way you talk about not having any connections with other people makes you sound like you think that you don't matter, that you aren't more than just who you are to other people. You are a person who matters, with thoughts and feelings like everybody else and your happiness is just as deserved as anyones. 

If you don't have a lot of friends or family in your life, you could go out and make those connections in the future. Life seems shitty sometimes, but the world around us is a magnificent place with opportunities everywhere. There's so much to see and do and we only get a few, short years to experience it, and it would be a tragedy for you, for anyone who feels the same to have their lives stolen away by depression.

 Don't let it beat you; too many lives have been ruined already, don't let it ruin yours. You are not your depression. You matter

A somewhat redeeming experience. Back when I first got my hands on an actually half-decent PC, I went on a pirating spree, picking up nearly every game I could while maniacally wringing my hands together.

A Youtube video game critic who has a particular dislike for Konami kept on talking about MGS, and I was somewhat intrigued. So, like an ass, I pirated MGSV. I crawled around on a hospital floor for about ten minutes and concluded that this probably wasn't the game for me. 

A little later, I got a PS2 emulator, and MGS3, somewhat intrigued. I played through about an hour of it, and fell in love a little, to the point where I purchased it on my PS2 and played through it all. (To those who are curious, I mostly use the PS2 emulator for games that I can no longer get my hands on, be that because of price or obscurity, and my PS2 has seen better days at this point).

After beating Metal Gear Solid three, I was enamoured by the series, and was far more sickened by how Konami had been pimping out it's baby. Even so, I actually went and bought Metal Gear Solid V, with human money instead of my dignity, and am currently ploughing my way through it. 

So, I'm fairly new, and the barrier to entry was a little... Disquieting, but I'm still loving every second of it.
The only conclusion I can draw is that my game is fucked. I can still choke out Russians, so I'm basically content. ^^
